title: Perl Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Print a greeting
examples.description: say prints text and adds a newline. The feature line enables it.

examples.title: Name a single value
examples.description: A scalar keeps one value. Its name starts with $. my declares the variable.

examples.title: Insert text values
examples.description: Double-quoted strings insert scalar variables into text.

examples.title: Keep an ordered list
examples.description: An array name starts with @. Read one item with $ and its zero-based position.

examples.title: Use text keys
examples.description: A hash pairs keys with values. Curly braces select a value by key.

examples.title: Choose an action
examples.description: if runs a block when the test is true.

examples.title: Compare text
examples.description: eq compares text. == is the numeric comparison operator.

examples.title: Visit each value
examples.description: for can visit each value in a list. The loop variable holds the current value.

examples.title: Name reusable steps
examples.description: A subroutine is a named set of steps. @_ holds its inputs.

examples.title: Find a text pattern
examples.description: A regular expression describes a pattern. =~ asks whether the string matches it.

examples.title: Replace matching text
examples.description: s/old/new/ replaces matching text. The g flag replaces all matches.

examples.title: Split and join text
examples.description: split breaks text at a pattern. join puts a list together with a separator.
